descriptionChirho: A constructed water channel, conduit, or trench used for conveying water. All senses refer to the same concrete referent — an artificial water passage — with variation only in grammatical form (singular, plural, construct, with article, with prepositions). Arabic consistently uses قَناة (qanah, 'canal/conduit'), Swahili uses mfereji/mifereji ('irrigation channel'), Korean alternates between 수로 (suro, 'waterway') and 도랑 (dorang, 'trench/ditch'), Hindi uses नाली/नाला ('drain/channel'), and Spanish uses canal/zanja ('canal/trench'). These are all inflectional and prepositional variants of a single lexical meaning: an engineered water passage.
